description: 🤗 Transformers: the model-definition framework for state-of-the-art machine learning models in text, vision, audio, and multimodal models, for both inference and training.

State-of-the-art pretrained models for inference and training

Transformers is the model-definition framework for machine learning models in text, computer vision, audio, video, and multimodal tasks. It defines each model once, in PyTorch, and you use that definition for both inference and training. Training frameworks, inference engines, and local runtimes build on that definition instead of writing their own. Transformers adds new architectures as they're released and matches each one to its original results, so those tools get each new model as soon as it's added.

Fine-tune with less memory. Unsloth trains LLMs in 4-bit, 8-bit, and 16-bit precision with custom kernels.
Serve LLMs at scale. vLLM batches requests continuously and keeps KV cache memory compact with PagedAttention.
Serve LLMs with low latency. SGLang is a high-throughput inference engine with a frontend language for agentic workflows.
Run LLMs locally without Python. llama.cpp is a C/C++ inference engine that runs quantized models in the GGUF format.
Transformers standardizes how every model is written, so hundreds of architectures share one structure. Each model is one file that reads from top to bottom and stays simple without giving up performance. An improvement made once reaches every architecture, so if you find one, [contribute it](./contributing). Transformers is designed to be read and modified by humans and coding agents alike. To swap how a model computes, register your own attention or experts function, or load an optimized kernel from the Hub, and the model uses it without edits to its code. ## Try a model Install Transformers with PyTorch. See the [Installation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/installation) guide for other setups. ```bash uv pip install "transformers[torch]" ``` Create a [`Pipeline`](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main_classes/pipelines) with a chat model from the [Hugging Face Hub](https://huggingface.co/models?library=transformers&sort=trending) and pass it a message. ```py from transformers import pipeline pipe = pipeline(task="text-generation", model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B") messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "What's the secret to baking a really good cake? Answer in one sentence."}, ] output = pipe(messages, tokenizer_encode_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False}) print(output[0]["generated_text"][-1]["content"]) # The secret to baking a really good cake is combining the perfect balance of ingredients, technique, and a warm, loving atmosphere. ``` The [Quickstart](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/quicktour) covers loading models, running inference on other tasks, and training. ## Set up your coding agent Copy the prompt below into your coding agent. It has the agent check your installed version, read the docs for that version, and use the current Transformers v5 APIs. ```text I'm building with Hugging Face Transformers. Before you write any Transformers code: 1. Check the installed version with `python -c "import transformers; print(transformers.__version__)"`. If Transformers isn't installed, install it with `pip install "transformers[torch]"`. 2. Read the docs index for that version at https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v/llms.txt, for example v5.22.2. For a .dev version, use https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/llms.txt. Add .md to any docs page URL to read it as Markdown. Look up each class and argument there instead of relying on memory. 3. If the version is 5.0 or later, read https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/MIGRATION_GUIDE_V5.md. Don't use APIs from older versions. 4. Read the model card of each model you use on the Hugging Face Hub. Many models need specific arguments, like a chat template option or a minimum Transformers version. ``` ## Run inference Load a pretrained model and run it on text, images, audio, video, or any combination of modalities. - [Pipeline](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pipeline_tutorial): Preprocess the input, run the model, and postprocess the output for a task with one class. - [Text generation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/llm_tutorial): Generate text with LLMs and VLMs, and control the decoding strategy and streaming. - [Chat with models](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/conversations): Start a chat in your terminal with `transformers chat`, or pass a chat history to a pipeline. ## Serve models Serve a model to other applications over HTTP. `transformers serve` is for evaluation, experimentation, and moderate load. For large production deployments, use an inference engine with a Transformers model as the backend. - [Serve CLI](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/serve-cli/serving): Start a local server compatible with the OpenAI SDK with `transformers serve`. - [Continuous batching](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/continuous_batching): Raise throughput by adding new requests to the batch as other requests finish. - [Inference engines](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/community_integrations/transformers_as_backend): Use a Transformers model as the backend for vLLM or SGLang. ## Train models Fine-tune a pretrained model on your data, on one GPU or many. - [Trainer](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/training): Run the training loop with support for mixed precision and `torch.compile`. - [PEFT](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/peft): Train a small adapter instead of all of a model's weights. - [FSDP](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/fsdp): Shard a model's parameters across GPUs to train models that don't fit on one. - [Tensor parallelism](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/tensor_parallelism): Split each weight matrix across GPUs so every GPU computes part of each layer. - [Expert parallelism](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/expert_parallelism): Place the experts of a mixture-of-experts model on different GPUs and route tokens to them. ## Use less memory and run faster Fit a model on your hardware and speed it up. - [Quantization](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/quantization/overview): Store weights in fewer bits so a model needs less memory. - [Kernels](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/kernel_doc/overview): Load precompiled operations for your hardware from the Hub. - [Attention backends](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/attention_interface): Switch between attention implementations without changing the model. ## Add or change a model Add a model to Transformers or edit an existing one. - [Modular Transformers](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/modular_transformers): Add a model by inheriting from existing models. A converter generates the standalone file. - [Model structure rules](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/modeling_rules): Follow the conventions a checker enforces on every modeling, modular, and configuration file. - [Writing model tests](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/testing): Write a small amount of model-specific test code, and the test mixins generate more than 100 tests from it. ## Citation We now have a [paper](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-demos.6/) you can cite for the 🤗 Transformers library: ```bibtex @inproceedings{wolf-etal-2020-transformers, title = "Transformers: State-of-the-Art Natural Language Processing", author = "Thomas Wolf and Lysandre Debut and Victor Sanh and Julien Chaumond and Clement Delangue and Anthony Moi and Pierric Cistac and Tim Rault and Rémi Louf and Morgan Funtowicz and Joe Davison and Sam Shleifer and Patrick von Platen and Clara Ma and Yacine Jernite and Julien Plu and Canwen Xu and Teven Le Scao and Sylvain Gugger and Mariama Drame and Quentin Lhoest and Alexander M. Try a model

Install Transformers with PyTorch. See the Installation guide for other setups.

uv pip install "transformers[torch]"

Create a Pipeline with a chat model from the Hugging Face Hub and pass it a message.

from transformers import pipeline

pipe = pipeline(task="text-generation", model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What's the secret to baking a really good cake? Answer in one sentence."},
]
output = pipe(messages, tokenizer_encode_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
print(output[0]["generated_text"][-1]["content"])
# The secret to baking a really good cake is combining the perfect balance of ingredients, technique, and a warm, loving atmosphere.

The Quickstart covers loading models, running inference on other tasks, and training.

Set up your coding agent

Copy the prompt below into your coding agent. It has the agent check your installed version, read the docs for that version, and use the current Transformers v5 APIs.

I'm building with Hugging Face Transformers. Before you write any Transformers code:

1. Check the installed version with `python -c "import transformers; print(transformers.__version__)"`. If Transformers isn't installed, install it with `pip install "transformers[torch]"`.
2. Read the docs index for that version at https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/v<version>/llms.txt, for example v5.22.2. For a .dev version, use https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/llms.txt. Add .md to any docs page URL to read it as Markdown. Look up each class and argument there instead of relying on memory.
3. If the version is 5.0 or later, read https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/MIGRATION_GUIDE_V5.md. Don't use APIs from older versions.
4. Read the model card of each model you use on the Hugging Face Hub. Many models need specific arguments, like a chat template option or a minimum Transformers version.

Run inference

Load a pretrained model and run it on text, images, audio, video, or any combination of modalities.

  • Pipeline: Preprocess the input, run the model, and postprocess the output for a task with one class.
  • Text generation: Generate text with LLMs and VLMs, and control the decoding strategy and streaming.
  • Chat with models: Start a chat in your terminal with transformers chat, or pass a chat history to a pipeline.

Serve models

Serve a model to other applications over HTTP. transformers serve is for evaluation, experimentation, and moderate load. For large production deployments, use an inference engine with a Transformers model as the backend.

  • Serve CLI: Start a local server compatible with the OpenAI SDK with transformers serve.
  • Continuous batching: Raise throughput by adding new requests to the batch as other requests finish.
  • Inference engines: Use a Transformers model as the backend for vLLM or SGLang.

Train models

Fine-tune a pretrained model on your data, on one GPU or many.

  • Trainer: Run the training loop with support for mixed precision and torch.compile.
  • PEFT: Train a small adapter instead of all of a model's weights.
  • FSDP: Shard a model's parameters across GPUs to train models that don't fit on one.
  • Tensor parallelism: Split each weight matrix across GPUs so every GPU computes part of each layer.
  • Expert parallelism: Place the experts of a mixture-of-experts model on different GPUs and route tokens to them.

Use less memory and run faster

Fit a model on your hardware and speed it up.

  • Quantization: Store weights in fewer bits so a model needs less memory.
  • Kernels: Load precompiled operations for your hardware from the Hub.
  • Attention backends: Switch between attention implementations without changing the model.

Add or change a model

Add a model to Transformers or edit an existing one.

  • Modular Transformers: Add a model by inheriting from existing models. A converter generates the standalone file.
  • Model structure rules: Follow the conventions a checker enforces on every modeling, modular, and configuration file.
  • Writing model tests: Write a small amount of model-specific test code, and the test mixins generate more than 100 tests from it.

releases.name: Patch release v5.24.1
releases.body:
# Patch release v5.24.1

A patch to fix a bunch of stuff for vLLM, a few distributed issues, and some model fixes (llama4, dory); see the full list

### vLLM related
- Fix backward compatibility of the cache rename for remote code (#51085) by @hmellor
- Restore modeling_attn_mask_utils for remote code (one-off to unblock vLLM) (#51124) by @hmellor 
- Expose past_key_values in MBartDecoderLayer.forward signature for remote code (#51177) by @hmellor 
- [OmniASR] Support a padding_mask kept on the CPU in the audio encoder (#51100) by @El-euchidali

### Model fixes
- Fix Llama4 forward crash on missing image_outputs (#51144) by @kylesayrs
- Fix dory static cache (#50993) by @ArthurZucker 

### Distributed
- Allow expert parallelism alone with tp_plan={} (#50996) by @3outeille 
- Fix strided checkpoint reads on PyTorch 2.9 (#51042) by @satsuki2486441738

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/compare/v5.24.0...v5.24.1

releases.name: Release v5.24.0
releases.body: # Release v5.24.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling 2 Mini Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is a smaller sibling of Inkling 2 Small, added in v5.23.0. It has 24 decoder layers instead of 48, and compensates with a looping mechanism in which layers 6 to 17 run three times. A learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and mixture-of-experts inputs of each loop layer. The decoder has a hidden size of 2304 and routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. The image encoder, tokenizer and processor are the same as Inkling 2 Small's. A research checkpoint ([TML-d24-varloop-research](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research)) has the same architecture but supports a variable number of loop passes. Fewer passes are faster, and more passes improve quality. Both checkpoints contain NVFP4 and MXFP8 quantized layers, which are dequantized at load time. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingfac

releases.name: Release v5.23.0
releases.body: # Release v5.23.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling2 Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/) * Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in [#50682](https://github.com/huggingface/transforme

aiSummary.oneLiner: State-of-the-art Machine Learning for PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Transformers provides thousands of pretrained models to perform tasks on different modalities such as text, vision, and audio. It offers a unified API that allows researchers and engineers to easily download, train, and deploy state-of-the-art models like BERT, GPT, and ViT. The library abstracts away the complex boilerplate required for distributed training and model inference across PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX. It deeply integrates with the Hugging Face Hub, facilitating seamless model sharing and version control for the machine learning community. This significantly reduces the compute costs and engineering time required to implement cutting-edge AI features in production.
keyFeatures: Unified API framework: Provides a consistent, simple interface to load and utilize thousands of different transformer architectures.
Multi-framework compatibility: Supports seamless interoperability and model conversion between PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX.
Pretrained model hub: Integrates directly with the Hugging Face Hub to instantly download state-of-the-art weights for NLP, vision, and audio.
Optimized training pipelines: Includes built-in classes like the Trainer API to drastically simplify distributed training and fine-tuning loops.
Extensive modality support: Handles complex multi-modal tasks including text classification, image segmentation, and automatic speech recognition.

useCases.title: Natural Language Processing
useCases.description: Deploy state-of-the-art text classification, summarization, and translation models directly into production applications with minimal code.

useCases.title: Model Fine-Tuning
useCases.description: Fine-tune massive pre-trained language models on proprietary, domain-specific datasets using optimized training pipelines.

useCases.title: Computer Vision Integration
useCases.description: Implement cutting-edge Vision Transformers for image classification or object detection without writing custom PyTorch architectures.

useCases.title: Cross-Framework Migration
useCases.description: Train a complex transformer model in PyTorch and easily export the weights for deployment in a highly optimized TensorFlow environment.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Machine learning engineers, AI researchers, and software developers who need to implement state-of-the-art AI models. It requires a solid understanding of machine learning concepts and familiarity with Python deep learning frameworks.
